question: can the macos-ax application campaign be executed on this host today, given that the campaign requires building two third-party macOS applications at two revisions each and launching all four?
method: attempt the campaign, and when the first launch does not return, characterise the failure directly: sample the stalled process, then run a bounded launch of ten deliberately different executables to find what separates the ones that run from the ones that do not

buildTrial.command: xcodebuild -project Platypus.xcodeproj -scheme Platypus -configuration Deployment CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY=- CODE_SIGN_STYLE=Manual DEVELOPMENT_TEAM= CODE_SIGNING_REQUIRED=NO CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO ENABLE_HARDENED_RUNTIME=NO SYMROOT=... OBJROOT=... CONFIGURATION_TEMP_DIR=... build
buildTrial.projectFinding: the project pins CONFIGURATION_TEMP_DIR to the empty string in every target, so a build fails with unable to write file '/platypus_clt.build/...' until SYMROOT, OBJROOT and CONFIGURATION_TEMP_DIR are all overridden on the command line. That is a real and fixable build recipe finding, and it is recorded because the next attempt should not rediscover it

buildTrial.stalledProcess: /bin/sh running the generated Script-F4302B7B21C5A04A001C8BEC.sh, sampled at 10m24s with the same _dyld_start signature and no children
buildTrial.note: /bin/sh is an Apple platform binary, so the build cannot be worked around by pre-warming the applications' own binaries: the stall reaches ordinary build script phases too
